newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks rise in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks rise in quiet trade.

text.p: Shares on the Amman stock exchange rose slightly for a second day in quiet trade on Monday but brokers said the bourse was still dogged by an apparent stalemate in Middle East peace talks.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.05 percent to 147.11 points from 147.03 points on Sunday.
"This was a natural reaction after the decreases of last week," said one broker. "Prices went down far below what was justified by the problems between Israel and the Palestinians."

But he said the Jordanian stock exchange, highly sensitive to Palestinian-Israeli talks and to growing doubts that neighbouring Iraq will be able to sell oil before the end of the year, remained subdued overall.
"The (low) volume of trade is an indication that we are putting ourselves on hold," he said.
Middle East Investment Bank and Arab Bank together accounted for a third of Monday's trade.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange rose 0.22 percent to 80.81 points from 80.63 points, still 15.39 percent down from the same time last year.
A total of 69,729 shares worth 46,640 dinars changed hands in thin trade in the parallel market.
